sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: Gausul Azam Maizbhandari Polytechnic Institute operated across five separate buildings with no unified network infrastructure. Each building ran independently with ad-hoc connectivity, leading to IP conflicts, no centralized monitoring, and frequent downtime affecting 700+ devices including computers, IP phones, CCTV cameras, printers, and IoT equipment.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I conducted a full site survey across all five buildings, mapped every access point, and designed a scalable network architecture from scratch. The implementation was done floor-by-floor to minimize disruption to daily classes.

steps.title: Survey & Planning
steps.desc: Mapped all 5 buildings, identified 700+ device endpoints, designed VLAN scheme and IP allocation strategy.

steps.title: Cabling & Infrastructure
steps.desc: Installed Cat6A and OS2 fiber backbone, patched all endpoints, set up distribution racks in each building.

steps.title: Configuration & VLANs
steps.desc: Configured MikroTik routers, set up 5+ VLANs (Office, Lab, College, Schools, Hostel), enabled DHCP, NAT, and VPN.

steps.title: Monitoring & Launch
steps.desc: Deployed PRTG for real-time monitoring, configured alerts, tested failover, and went live building by building.

architecture.title: Campus Network Topology
architecture.desc: 5 Buildings · 3 Distribution Racks · Core Router · 5+ VLANs · Fiber Backbone

highlights.title: Structured Cabling
highlights.desc: Cat6A copper and OS2 fiber backbone connecting all 5 buildings with redundancy.

highlights.title: Wi-Fi 6E Coverage
highlights.desc: Wireless access points across all buildings with zone-based security and roaming.

highlights.title: VLAN Segmentation
highlights.desc: 5+ VLANs isolating Office, Lab, College, Schools, and Hostel traffic.

highlights.title: Real-time Monitoring
highlights.desc: PRTG dashboard with device tracking, bandwidth alerts, and uptime reports.

highlights.title: Zone-based Security
highlights.desc: Firewall rules, NAT, and VPN access for remote management.

highlights.title: 700+ Devices Connected
highlights.desc: Computers, IP phones, CCTV cameras, printers, and IoT devices — all managed centrally.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: The campus now operates on a unified, scalable network with 99.8% uptime. IP conflicts are eliminated through proper VLAN segmentation and DHCP reservations. The IT team can monitor all 700+ devices from a single PRTG dashboard, reducing troubleshooting time by 40%. The infrastructure is ready for future expansion with fiber backbone capacity.

sections.title: Configuration Snippet
sections.configNote: MikroTik VLAN configuration for building segmentation:

config.code:
# Create VLAN interfaces
/interface vlan add name=vlan10-office vlan-id=10 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan20-lab vlan-id=20 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan30-college vlan-id=30 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan40-schools vlan-id=40 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan50-hostel vlan-id=50 interface=ether1

# DHCP Networks
/ip dhcp-server network add address=10.10.10.0/24 gateway=10.10.10.1 dns-server=8.8.8.8
/ip dhcp-server network add address=10.10.20.0/24 gateway=10.10.20.1 dns-server=8.8.8.8

# Firewall Rules
/ip firewall filter add chain=forward src-address=10.10.10.0/24 action=accept
/ip firewall filter add chain=forward src-address=10.10.20.0/24 action=accept

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: The polytechnic's computer labs needed a complete overhaul. Outdated workstations, unreliable network connectivity, and frequent hardware failures were causing regular session delays for students. There was no standardized imaging, no preventive maintenance schedule, and the LAN infrastructure was unstable — affecting daily practical classes across all three labs.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I managed the end-to-end deployment from hardware assembly to network setup, ensuring every workstation was ready for daily use with zero downtime during practical sessions.

steps.title: Hardware Assembly & Imaging
steps.desc: Assembled 30+ PC workstations from components, installed OS images, configured drivers, and deployed to lab stations.

steps.title: LAN Infrastructure
steps.desc: Executed RJ-45 Cat6 cabling, patch panel crimping, switch configuration, and static/dynamic IP allocations across all workstations.

steps.title: Diagnostics & Testing
steps.desc: Performed stress testing, bench diagnostics, and validated each workstation before going live to ensure reliability.

steps.title: Preventive Maintenance
steps.desc: Established routine maintenance schedules, dust cleaning, driver updates, and performance monitoring for long-term lab health.

architecture.title: Lab Network Topology
architecture.desc: 30+ Workstations · 2 Core Switches · Patch Panel · Cat6 Cabling · DHCP Server

highlights.title: Full Hardware Assembly
highlights.desc: Built 30+ PCs from components — motherboards, RAM, storage, PSUs — tested before deployment.

highlights.title: Cat6 LAN Cabling
highlights.desc: Complete RJ-45 crimping, patch panel wiring, and switch configuration for all workstations.

highlights.title: 25% Downtime Reduction
highlights.desc: Standardized imaging and preventive maintenance eliminated recurring hardware failures.

highlights.title: Zero Session Delays
highlights.desc: Every workstation validated before class — no more student waiting during practical sessions.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: All three labs now run a combined 50+ workstations with zero session delays for daily practical classes. Downtime reduced by 25% through standardized imaging and preventive maintenance. Each lab has its own subnet for organized network management, and the maintenance schedule ensures long-term reliability across all labs.

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: The campus had no centralized surveillance system. Computer labs, classrooms, and administrative areas were unmonitored, creating security vulnerabilities. There was no recording infrastructure, no motion detection, and no way to review incidents after the fact.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I planned the camera placement strategy, managed the cabling infrastructure, and configured the entire surveillance system from hardware mounting to centralized monitoring.

steps.title: Site Survey & Planning
steps.desc: Surveyed all buildings, identified critical zones, planned camera angles and coverage areas for maximum visibility.

steps.title: Camera Installation
steps.desc: Mounted HD IP cameras across labs, classrooms, and admin areas with strategic positioning for full coverage.

steps.title: NVR & Storage Setup
steps.desc: Installed centralized NVR units, configured storage drives, set up motion-detection triggers and recording schedules.

steps.title: Cabling & Monitoring
steps.desc: Managed Ethernet cable routing, connector termination, and configured centralized monitoring screens for security staff.

architecture.desc: HD IP Cameras · NVR Units · Motion Detection · Centralized Monitoring · 24/7 Recording

highlights.title: HD IP Cameras
highlights.desc: High-definition surveillance cameras with night vision and wide-angle coverage.

highlights.title: Centralized NVR Storage
highlights.desc: Network Video Recorders with redundant storage for continuous 24/7 recording.

highlights.title: Motion Detection
highlights.desc: AI-powered motion triggers with configurable sensitivity and alert zones.

highlights.title: Centralized Monitoring
highlights.desc: Dedicated monitoring station with multi-screen display for real-time campus surveillance.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: The campus now has complete surveillance coverage across all critical areas. The system records 24/7 with motion-detection alerts, enabling rapid response to incidents. Centralized monitoring allows security staff to oversee the entire campus from a single station. The infrastructure supports future expansion with additional cameras and storage capacity.

config.code:
# Motion Detection Configuration
motion_detection:
  enabled: true
  sensitivity: medium
  zones:
    - name: "computer-lab"
      cameras: [cam-01, cam-02, cam-03]
      schedule: "24/7"
      alerts: [email, push]
    - name: "classroom"
      cameras: [cam-04, cam-05]
      schedule: "08:00-18:00"
      alerts: [push]
    - name: "admin-area"
      cameras: [cam-06]
      schedule: "24/7"
      alerts: [email, push]

# Recording Schedule
recording:
  mode: "continuous"
  retention_days: 30
  resolution: "1080p"
  fps: 25

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: Institute attendance was being recorded manually on paper registers every day. The system had no central record, so calculating a student's present percentage meant counting dozens of register pages by hand. Paper registers were also easy to mark attendance for someone who was not present, and there was no reliable proof of attendance to support exam eligibility. Compiling the monthly report consumed a large part of the office's administrative time.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I selected and deployed two biometric attendance terminals, connected them to the attendance database over the campus LAN, and handled the full enrolment and reporting workflow — from mounting the hardware to producing the monthly attendance report.

steps.title: Device Selection & Placement
steps.desc: Selected two ZKTeco terminals supporting fingerprint, face recognition, and RFID card verification. Placed one at the main entrance for students and a second at the office entrance for teachers and staff, keeping the two groups on separate devices.

steps.title: Installation & Network Setup
steps.desc: Mounted both terminals, wired them into the campus LAN with Cat6, and assigned static IP addresses so the attendance server could reach each device reliably instead of depending on DHCP leases.

steps.title: Enrolment & Data Sync
steps.desc: Enrolled 300+ students and 40+ teaching and support staff across fingerprint, face, and RFID methods, then connected both devices to the ZKTime/ZKBio attendance database so records pushed automatically.

steps.title: Reporting Integration
steps.desc: Configured scheduled time synchronisation so device clocks never drifted, and set up the ZKTime reporting workflow so the monthly attendance report could be generated and exported instead of compiled by hand.

architecture.title: Attendance System Layout
architecture.desc: 2 ZKTeco Terminals · Static IP on Campus LAN · ZKTime/ZKBio Database · Scheduled Reports

highlights.title: Multi-Modal Verification
highlights.desc: Fingerprint, face recognition, and RFID card — so a damaged finger or a forgotten card does not stop someone being marked present.

highlights.title: Separate Student & Staff Devices
highlights.desc: Two dedicated terminals keep the large student population and the smaller staff population on independent, clearly separated records.

highlights.title: Static IP on Campus LAN
highlights.desc: Both terminals hold fixed addresses, so the attendance server connects to them reliably with no manual reconnection after a power cut.

highlights.title: Automated Monthly Reports
highlights.desc: Attendance data pushes to the database continuously, so the monthly report is generated rather than assembled by hand.

sections.title: Maintenance Routine
sections.content:
Ongoing work to keep both terminals accurate and reporting reliably:

  • Biometric Enrolment — enrolling new students and staff, and re-enrolling when a template fails to read
  • Template Backup — backing up fingerprint and face templates after every enrolment batch so a device failure is recoverable
  • Time Synchronisation — monitoring clock drift and keeping both terminals on the correct network time
  • Log Export & Sync Troubleshooting — resolving failed pushes to the database and correcting wrong times in exported reports
  • Firmware Updates — applying device firmware updates and adding new users to the database
  • Sensor Cleaning — routine cleaning of the fingerprint sensor, camera lens, and RFID reader surface

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Attendance for 300+ students and 40+ staff is now captured automatically at the point of entry, with no paper registers in the process. Because every record is tied to a biometric or card identity, marking attendance for someone who is not present is no longer possible. Records are available centrally as they are captured rather than reconstructed at month end, which removed most of the manual work from the monthly attendance report.
